```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ocular` retrieves satellite imagery and calculates spectral indices for crop
monitoring and agricultural research, including vegetative indices (VI).
This guide takes one query through field boundary delineation to a raster and
a time series. Install using the [README instructions](https://github.com/AAGI-AUS/ocular#installation),
then load the package:

```{r load-ocular}
library(ocular)
```

If your installation includes built vignettes, `browseVignettes("ocular")`
opens the guides locally. The links in this guide open their repository sources.

The retrieval examples need internet access to the Microsoft Planetary Computer
Data Catalog. They are not executed when this guide is built.

## Retrieve imagery

Choose a point inside the intended field, a date range, and the size of the
surrounding analysis area. Coordinates are longitude and latitude in WGS 84.
Here `x_metres = 1000` sets a 1,000 m square; supply `y_metres` for a different
height. Both dates are inclusive.

```{r retrieve-scenes, eval=FALSE}
rs <- get_rs(
  longitude = -96.80342,
  latitude = 33.26425,
  start_date = "2005-03-15",
  end_date = "2005-09-05",
  x_metres = 1000,
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-5"
)

rs
```

Printing the `ocular` object reports the source, scene count and mask-cell
count when available. The object keeps the retrieved scenes, query and settings. Keep `rs`
as the starting point for comparing workflows.

Detection features and calibration are prepared when delineation needs them.
You can use `rs` directly for raster or time-series extraction.

## Delineate and inspect a field

`boundary_delineation()` uses the supplied point as a seed and compares
spectral values across dates. It stores a candidate field mask on the returned
object. It does not classify crop production status; check the result for your
location and intended use.

```{r delineate-and-convert, eval=FALSE}
field <- boundary_delineation(rs)
field

vi_raster <- as_raster(field)
vi_series <- as_time_series(field)

terra::plot(vi_raster)
head(vi_series)
```

| Output | Default contents |
|---|---|
| `vi_raster` | A `terra::SpatRaster`: median NDVI at each retained pixel across the retrieved scenes. |
| `vi_series` | A data frame: `date` and `value`, with mean NDVI within the field for each available day. |

The series includes available dates, not a complete daily calendar. These
values describe the selected imagery and mask, not a validated field boundary.
For monthly or yearly summaries, see `time_aggregate` in `?as_time_series`.

Daily dates are returned as text in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Use `as.Date()` for
a date axis in base R:

```{r plot-daily-series, eval=FALSE}
if( nrow(vi_series) > 0L ){
  plot(as.Date(vi_series$date), vi_series$value,
       type = "p", xlab = "Date", ylab = "Mean NDVI")
}
```

Save the outputs using their usual R interfaces:

```{r save-outputs, eval=FALSE}
terra::writeRaster(vi_raster, "field-ndvi.tif")
write.csv(vi_series, "field-ndvi.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### If the result is empty or unexpected

- **No scenes were retrieved:** check the source, dates, location and
  `max_cloud_cover`. No-scenes errors are different from an empty delineation.
- **Detection features could not be prepared:** `rs` still contains the output
  observations. Use `as_raster(rs)` or `as_time_series(rs)` for extraction.
  For delineation, review the reported detection dates and available imagery.
- **No candidate field was identified:** the raster is all `NA` and the series
  has no rows. Check the point and imagery. Use a new `get_rs()` call to change
  the point, dates or retrieval filters; reuse `rs` to compare delineation
  settings. An unchanged call will repeat the same analysis.
  An empty mask is not replaced by the full analysis area.
- **The mask is nonempty but some dates or values are absent:** cloud/quality
  exclusions or missing index data can leave no finite values inside it.
  Such dates are omitted from the series.
- **The candidate boundary is unsuitable:** inspect the full analysis-area
  raster below and compare workflows in the
  [delineation guide](https://github.com/AAGI-AUS/ocular/blob/main/vignettes/ocular-build-pipeline.Rmd). A new parameter comparison
  should start from `rs`, rather than repeatedly modifying `field`.

## Choose the area to summarise

Use the retrieved object directly for the full analysis area:

```{r full-analysis-area, eval=FALSE}
analysis_raster <- as_raster(rs)
analysis_series <- as_time_series(rs)
terra::plot(analysis_raster)
```

If you already have a field polygon, use it directly as an output mask. No
field boundary delineation or GeoParquet prior is needed. The `sf` or `sfc`
geometry must be nonempty and have a defined coordinate reference system.

```{r supplied-mask, eval=FALSE}
# field_boundary is your sf or sfc polygon object
vi_raster <- as_raster(rs, mask = field_boundary)
vi_series <- as_time_series(rs, mask = field_boundary)
```

If you have an independent reference boundary for the field and study period,
compare it with the candidate:

```{r compare-reference, eval=FALSE}
diagnose_against_ftw(field, reference = field_boundary)
```

You must supply a suitable reference; ocular does not retrieve one or check
its date. A boundary used to guide delineation or choose settings is not
independent. See `?diagnose_against_ftw` for the agreement metrics.

## Adapt the retrieval to your study

**Source.** Set `source` explicitly for a consistent sensor family:
`"sentinel-2"`, `"landsat-8"` (Landsat 8/9), or `"landsat-5"` (Landsat 5/7).
The default `"auto"` chooses one family from the start date; see `?get_rs`.
For duplicate Sentinel-2 products from the same acquisition and tile, ocular
keeps the highest available processing baseline by default. `s2_processing`
in `?rs_params` describes the alternative and incomplete-metadata handling.

**Clouds and quality.** `max_cloud_cover` filters whole scenes using catalogue
metadata. It does not mask pixels. `scl_classes` optionally excludes Sentinel-2
SCL class values or Landsat `QA_PIXEL` bit positions; the default `NULL` applies
no per-pixel mask. Choose exclusions for the selected sensor; its class or bit
numbers are not interchangeable with another sensor's.

**Indices and dates.** `index_name` controls the output values. Delineation uses
`search_index` (`"EVI2"` by default) to construct a multi-temporal spectral
feature stack. `search_start_date` and `search_end_date` can restrict that
boundary evidence within the retrieval period without removing output dates.
See `?get_rs` for supported indices and arguments.
